reason: Closed only 'with' the Bonferroni and Lucas constructions it inspired; no attempt ever tested its own translation, that in the replica-symmetric regime the allowed set (or a typical subset) is itself a top-lift subset. That target is exactly the current conj:lagged-lift-subset, so the closure is by association, not by a reason the attempt found.
next_attempt: Use the replica-symmetric/contiguity picture directly: compare a random-prefix family's allowed set with the base P (where the lift is known) and test the lagged-lift criterion (prop:lagged-lift-criterion) on the allowed set itself, or on a random subset of it, for the smallest dense families beyond capacity.

reason: Developed into lem:lucas-truncation and prop:lucas-multiplier-reduction; prop:hiding-needs-emptiness proved that the hiding condition needs empty deep overlaps, at degree of order n*s, beyond any design range. The budget review shows this barrier covers every pointwise multiplier, and the remaining route records that the colon form also stays pointwise on the PHP-hard part. This is a falsification covering the idea, not one formulation.

The test already found that it is the record's A3 heuristic in the source's language, and the design-route review confirmed it gives no mechanism for A1. Restating the open problem is a listed closure reason; A3 itself is tracked as an open statement (conj:semi-regular-relative-to-base).

A rate bound could only sharpen the exchange-rate barrier for pointwise/base-design multipliers. The colon multipliers entry showed those certificates are pointwise on the PHP-hard part, a programme recorded as exhausted. No current open statement asks for a barrier, so the result would have no remaining application.

Its test located the failure of distributivity purely in the degree filtration, and batched splitting identified that filtration failure as a fall, a first syzygy of the sum of the members' tops. What is left is the Tor-vanishing statement itself, so the closure is a restatement of the open problem.

Developed only into a necessary condition (Frobenius splitting, conj:uniform-level-balance), then closed because sufficiency would need a special-position Dade lemma that the truncated counterexample rules out 'in general'. The bridge's actual proposal, a code-distance-type bound on the degree at which shifted directions can fail freeness, was never attempted. A general counterexample does not rule out special position for the actual instances, and row freeness on the allowed set (conj:closed-row-freeness) remains a current route to W.
open_statement: W via conj:closed-row-freeness (row freeness on the allowed set, column forms at density >= 1/2)
next_attempt: Formulate a joint, multi-direction distance statement (no low-degree combination of shifted row-sum directions acts trivially on functions on the allowed set), and test whether the truncated Dade counterexample's special position can occur on allowed sets of density >= 1/2 under random prefixes.

reason: Developed into two working proofs (thm:shared-cell-induction, thm:pair-reduction), then superseded by thm:bounded-clusters, which settles the designed case without link induction. Supersession by a stronger result is a listed reason, and the designed case of A2/A3 is recorded as settled.

Its only purpose was to raise the clause count at fixed lambda. Under thm:bounded-clusters lambda may grow to a constant fraction of k, and the explicit column design gives every polynomial count without packings. Superseded; nothing in the open statements depends on the count.

Proposed counting pattern choices for each level of the link induction. The component count of thm:bounded-clusters replaced the induction, so the counting it proposed is subsumed. This is supersession, with no remaining target.

Developed in the coarse-graining barrier: prop:coarse-graining-barrier proves that support-level coarse-graining leaves a delta^2 fraction of a dense family in one group, a falsification of the support form. The coefficient-level form was carried on as conj:pseudorandom-taylor / conj:column-weight-taylor and developed in later entries, so the idea is not lost.

Its test already reduced it to linear algebra (a vector set avoids every proper subspace iff it spans), and it was absorbed into prop:relation-avoidance. For classes on many tops spanning fails by dimension, so the tool is inapplicable there. A restatement plus inapplicability, found by the attempt.

Developed into prop:stopping-set-survival (survivor supports are stopping sets of about n^2/(K log_3 n) tops for random families). The remaining part, bounding supports of base classes, was the line's obstacle itself. A later LDPC bridge carried the coding view forward. Developed, then a restatement.

Its soundness bound is exactly cor:defect-decay's factor 3 per cell, and its derandomization is the spanning condition, both inside prop:relation-avoidance. The review found that the factor-3 count decides nothing by itself. The translation's content is fully absorbed: a restatement.

Developed in group freeness and base-union socle: the expected Hilbert function for single tops and pairs is proved on one row. The many-generator case is, by prop:batched-splitting, the Tor-vanishing open statement itself, so closing as a restatement is legitimate. The later Fröberg lead (convergence-review:2) is the queue's vehicle for the random case; see that item.

Under a split the vectors to avoid have weight at most 2, so the needed null-space property is the column-weight condition at t=2, absorbed into prop:split-obstruction-bound. The open part is the split itself. The translation is fully absorbed (restatement).

Developed in colon pieces: pieces lie in relative socles, but the colon counts cells and cannot separate directions by weight, and a vanishing colon on small bases is contradicted by the data. A real development with a falsification of what the lead needed.

Its own test already found that the translation is exactly prop:split-obstruction-bound and adds no mechanism for the split. The closure is a restatement of a proved proposition. The split line is not among the current open statements.

Developed in column-support freeness (prop:sequential-freeness) and tested in relation-length syzygies. Its hypothesis fails for every single linear relation among three tops (ex:three-top-relation-types), and the prefix rule cannot avoid planted relations. This falsification covers the use for W's global step.

Never worked for nine reviews. Its single development (configuration review) found tensor families with relation span c*log_3(2X+1), as predicted, and explicitly left open whether the pinned-rank reduction handles rank of order c log n. It was then closed because the route moved to the base's image, which is not a reason the attempt found, while that check still bears on settling a class of adversarial families.
next_attempt: Check whether the pinned-rank reduction (pinned-rank vacuity) extends from rank O(c) to span rank O(c log n) within W's budget. If it does, the LCC dimension bound settles all relation-rich families, and the remaining case is families with O(1) relations per block.

reason: The direct-sum case is lem:kunneth-component-locality, already recorded. The non-direct-sum case was handed to the density-evolution lead, whose girth form was then refuted by the degree-zero circuits, and the content was carried into the Mayer–Vietoris/cluster theorem. This is a closure chain ending in supersession and falsification.

Developed into prop:square-syzygy-reduction, which proves the defects these identities give, including the projective-line class. Nothing later depends on them. Developed, with no remaining application.

Undeveloped for many cycles. The only work recorded the tensor and forced families as circuits of the omega-matroid and observed that a count by span alone cannot predict them; no Laman-type count was attempted beyond that. It was closed because dependencies are 'absorbed by dense members' under conj:dense-cover-generation, a conjecture of a route since moved on, so the circuit count still bears on Tor vanishing for adversarial tops.
open_statement: A1/A3 (Tor vanishing for adversarial clause tops: which dependency structures carry non-local classes)
next_attempt: Formulate a weighted Laman-type count (members weighted by h, relations by their degree) that separates the tensor and forced circuits from a lifted spread of equal span. Test it on the recorded circuits and on the chain and triangle data.

reason: Developed by local Taylor generation and planted locality, with exact additivity in 1544 subfamilies. Its girth form was then refuted by the degree-zero circuits, which break locality at degree 0, and its content moved into the Mayer–Vietoris sequence and the cluster theorem. Falsification plus supersession.

Developed into thm:cluster-sequential-freeness and prop:linear-transversality, which reduce locality to the per-block Tor condition, the open statement itself. Developed to the point where its remaining content is the open problem.

Developed into cor:pinned-cluster-reduction (one renormalization step). The iterated version was examined in the dense-cover review: iterated pinning beyond capacity is per-block removal, whose linear ceiling is recorded. That covers the idea beyond its first step.

Developed through the treewidth bridge, with exact images on chains, a star and a triangle. thm:coordinate-relation-locality showed the cyclic triangle is generated by edges, so acyclicity is not the governing invariant. The dense core's relation hypergraphs are cyclic anyway, so the sufficient direction has no application there. A falsification found by the attempt.

The configuration review found that for adversarial blocks with h=k+1 the prefixes supply no genericity, which falsifies the A1 use only. The closing text itself says 'the lead remains relevant to random forms (A3)'. Closing while the translation still bears on a current open statement violates the squeeze rule.
open_statement: A3 (Tor vanishing through degree 22k for random tops; per-block Hilbert-series identity)
next_attempt: Apply proved cases of Fröberg-type statements (e.g. Hochster–Laksov maximal rank in the first nontrivial degree) to the per-block Hilbert-series identity for random tops at degrees h+1, h+2. Check them against the recorded random-top computations (generic directness).

reason: Closed after one cycle on a structural remark (locality needs bounded geometric dimension), which applies to the Bravyi–Terhal no-go application, not to the cleaning lemma as an erasure-correctability tool. Its degree-h case is prop:cross-block-weight. The proposed higher-degree cleaning argument was never attempted in nine reviews, and the per-block Tor condition it targets remains on the route ('blocks as clusters need the same Tor vanishing per block').
open_statement: A2/A3 (per-block Tor vanishing for tops, blocks as clusters)
next_attempt: Attempt the degree h+1 cleaning step: show that if no short cross-block combination lies in V_b*A (prop:cross-block-weight) then I cap V_b*A has no new elements in degree h+1, cleaning a candidate off the block's forms. Test on the shared-square circuit.

reason: Closed by a one-step objection, 'direct form vacuous (cells are single-top)', after which its content 'became' conj:span-local-generation, the conjecture the matching was meant to prove. No acyclic matching was attempted on a complex whose cells are members or member unions, and a matching mechanism for generation by members still bears on Tor vanishing with members as units.
open_statement: A1/A3 (Tor vanishing / generation of clause-top syzygies by members as units)
next_attempt: Build an acyclic matching (Jöllenbeck–Welker/Sköldberg) on the Taylor complex of the clause tops, grouped by member (e.g. a Lyubeznik-type matching ordered by member). Check whether its critical 1-cells are member-supported on the chain, triangle and tensor families.

reason: Developed: its predicted ring corrections were found as the covering triples of stars, and chains showed none, matching the data. The pattern-level mechanism is carried by thm:star-family-locality and thm:adapted-helly-locality, so the bridge has no separate open question.

Developed into thm:involvement-threshold and prop:group-freeness's superadditivity. prop:relation-merging-barrier then proves that tensor superadditivity certifies only a small fraction of the relations beyond capacity. A proved barrier for the dense core.

Developed into thm:adapted-helly-locality. Two formulations were then falsified for the dense core: by shared coordinates the Helly number is unbounded, and by span intersections the tensor members meet pairwise in 0 yet their dependency needs all (3^{c+1}-1)/2 of them. Falsification by a concrete family.
Developed into lem:socle-onset-criterion. The socle question it raised on quotients is superseded by the relation-space Hilbert criterion of prop:relation-merging-barrier. Developed, then superseded.
